    ## Twin Comparison

    ```{python}
    import pandas as pd
    import altair as alt

    # Load data
    url = "https://calvin-data304.netlify.app/data/twins-genetics-wide.json"
    url2 = "https://calvin-data304.netlify.app/data/twins-genetics-long.json"
    genetics_wide = pd.read_json(url)
    genetics_long = pd.read_json(url2)
    ```

    ```{python}
    chart = alt.Chart(genetics_long).transform_filter(
        alt.FieldEqualPredicate(field='kit', equal='Ancestry')).mark_bar().encode(
        x=alt.X("id:N", title="Twin"),
        y=alt.Y("genetic share:Q", title="Genetic Share", axis=alt.Axis(format='%')),
        color=alt.Color("region:N", title="ID").scale(scheme = "dark2"),
        column=alt.Column("pair:N", title="Pair")
    ).properties(
        width=80,
        height=300,
        title="Comparison of Genetic Share for Twin Pairs using Ancestry kit"
    )

    chart
    ```

    The graph visualizes genetic share of a total of six pairs of twin which shows their region ancestry data percentage. Each column in the graph represents a pair of twins, with bars grouped and colored by the region. From the graph, a conclusion can be taken that for most of these pairs, to be specific, pair 1, 3, and 5 has identical result for both A and B twin. Whereas the rest of them has a slight different percentages that is present.

    ## Kit Comparison

```{python}
chart = alt.Chart(genetics_long).mark_bar().encode(
    x=alt.X("id:N", title="Twin"),
    y=alt.Y("genetic share:Q", title="Genetic Share", axis=alt.Axis(format='%')),
    color=alt.Color("region:N", title="region").scale(scheme = "set1"),
    column=alt.Column("pair:N", title="Pair"),
    row=alt.Row("kit", title="Kit")
).properties(
    width=80,
    height=300,
    title="Comparison of Genetic Share for Twin Pairs using Ancestry kit"
)

chart
```

The graph presents a comparison of genetic share test result of six pairs of twin that uses three different kits including 23andMe, Ancestry, and MyHeritage. The graph colored the genetic each pair have across different regions. Based on this graph, I want it to tell a story where it can show how different kits can result in different region percentages. For example, just from the first pair of twins alone, not only that MyHeritage differs the percentage of SE Europe in the pair but pair A and pair B is quite distinctive. In addition to this, this comparison of kits can be helpful to see which might be most accurate. It was quite obvious that Ancestry is the reliable option based on the total of genetic share that sums up to 100%.
